bib.title: QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

question: Can a frozen 4-bit quantized LLM be finetuned through LoRA adapters without losing 16-bit finetuning quality, and how good a chatbot does that make at 7B to 65B scale?
hypothesis: Performance lost to 4-bit quantization can be recovered by adapter finetuning, so 4-bit QLoRA with NF4 matches 16-bit full finetuning and 16-bit LoRA.
contributions: 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a data type information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights
Double Quantization, quantizing the quantization constants
Paged Optimizers using NVIDIA unified memory to manage memory spikes
Guanaco model family and a study of 1,000+ finetuned models across 8 instruction datasets, with human and GPT-4 chatbot evaluation

method.summary: A pretrained model is quantized to 4-bit NF4 with double quantization and frozen; LoRA adapters on all linear layers are trained in BF16 by backpropagating through the dequantized weights, with paged optimizer states. Evaluated against 16-bit LoRA and full finetuning (RoBERTa, T5, LLaMA) and used to finetune LLaMA 7B-65B on eight instruction datasets, judged by MMLU, GPT-4 and human raters.
method.task: instruction finetuning / parameter-efficient finetuning of quantized LLMs; chatbot evaluation

datasets.name: OASST1
datasets.size: 9,209 examples (top reply per level; 161,443 messages, 66,497 conversations)
datasets.split: full conversation incl. user queries; validation set used as OA benchmark
datasets.preprocessing: only the top reply at each level of the conversation tree

datasets.name: HH-RLHF
datasets.preprocessing: helpfulness and harmlessness combined, only the preferred reply kept

datasets.name: FLAN v2
datasets.preprocessing: same task mixtures as the authors except some datasets not freely available; subsampled in ablations

datasets.name: Alpaca
datasets.source: distilled from GPT-3 Instruct and ChatGPT

datasets.name: Longform
datasets.source: C4, Wikipedia, Stack Exchange, WikiHow plus LLM-generated instructions

datasets.name: Super-NaturalInstructions
datasets.split: training data split into training and validation for tuning and early stopping
datasets.preprocessing: same preprocessing as Wang et al. [60]

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.split: 5-shot test accuracy; 5-shot dev set used for validation and hyperparameter tuning

datasets.name: OA benchmark (OASST1 validation)
datasets.split: all user messages in validation set, previous turns in prompt

models.name: Guanaco
models.architecture: LLaMA + QLoRA adapters finetuned on OASST1

models.name: Vicuna 13B, Open Assistant 33B, GPT-3.5-turbo, Bard, GPT-4

training.objective: cross-entropy loss (supervised), response only where instruction/response are separate; no RL
training.optimizer: Adam with beta2 0.999, paged optimizer states
training.batch_size: 16 for 7B/13B; 32 or 16 for 33B; 64, 16 or 32 for 65B (Table 9, depends on dataset)
training.seq_len: source 384 / target 128 (All); OASST1 target 512; HH-RLHF target 768; Longform source 512 / target 1024
training.precision: NF4 storage with double quantization, bf16 computation datatype
training.dropout: LoRA dropout 0.1 for models up to 13B and 0.05 for 33B and 65B
training.regularisation: max grad norm of 0.3; group-by-length batching
training.hardware: single 24 GB consumer GPU (33B) or single 48 GB professional GPU (65B); Hyak supercomputer at University of Washington
training.compute: 33B Guanaco in less than 12 hours on a 24 GB GPU; 65B in 24 hours on one professional GPU; more than 1,000 models trained
training.seeds: Fig 2: one run per random seed; Fig 4: 3 random seeds per hyperparameter combination

other.lora: r = 64, alpha = 16, LoRA on all linear layers (chatbot runs); for Super-NaturalInstructions r = 16 (small/medium/large T5) or 64 (xl/xxl), alpha = 64, no dropout
other.nf4_blocksize: blocksize 64 for weights W, 256 for second-level constants c2 (FP8)
other.lora_search: dropout {0.0, 0.05, 0.1}; r {8,16,32,64,128,256}; layers {key+query, all attention, all FFN, all, attention+FFN output}; LoRA alpha fixed, learning rate searched
other.full_finetune_baseline_search: learning rates 1e-6 to 5e-5 and batch sizes 8 to 128
other.scaling: all 7B hyperparameters generalize to 13B/33B except learning rate and batch size; learning rate halved and batch size doubled for 33B and 65B

inference.samples: GPT-4 scoring reported as mean over both response orders; Elo averaged over 10,000 random orderings
inference.prompting: MMLU 5-shot; Vicuna benchmark GPT-4 scores both responses out of ten with explanation; pairwise GPT-4 picks best or tie

metrics.name: Vicuna benchmark score relative to ChatGPT
metrics.definition: GPT-4 scores both responses out of ten; model score as percentage of ChatGPT's, mean over both orders

metrics.name: Elo
metrics.definition: tournament of pairwise human or GPT-4 judgments, start 1000, K = 32, 10,000 random orderings

metrics.name: Mean zero-shot accuracy / Pile Common Crawl PPL
metrics.definition: quantization data type comparison over OPT, BLOOM, LLaMA, Pythia 125M-13B

eval.protocol: Human raters on Amazon Mechanical Turk (2 annotators vs ChatGPT, 3 for pairwise) plus GPT-4 judge; no significance test reported beyond 95% CIs

availability.weights: adapters for 7/13/33/65B trained on 8 datasets (32 models) released
availability.data: model generations with human and GPT-4 annotations released

results.claim: Guanaco 65B reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's Vicuna-benchmark score with 24 hours of finetuning on one professional GPU.
results.setup: Guanaco 65B (4-bit, OASST1), GPT-4 judge, 80 Vicuna prompts, mean over both orders, 95% CI 4.4%
results.quote: achieve 99.3% with our largest model, essentially
results.note: Table 6 gives 99.3% with 95% CI 4.4%; confidence intervals overlap with many models.

results.claim: Regular 16-bit finetuning of LLaMA 65B needs more than 780 GB GPU memory; QLoRA brings it under 48 GB.
results.quote: requires more than 780 GB of GPU memory

results.claim: Double Quantization saves about 0.373 bits per parameter (about 3 GB at 65B).
results.setup: blocksize 64 for weights, 32-bit constants quantized to FP8 with blocksize 256
results.note: Introduction rounds it to about 0.37 bits

results.claim: On LLaMA 7B-65B finetuned on Alpaca and FLAN v2, NF4+DQ matches BF16 LoRA on mean MMLU while FP4 is about a point behind.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B/13B/33B/65B x Alpaca/FLAN v2, adapters; BF16 53.0, Float4 52.2, NFloat4+DQ 53.1
results.table: Table 4, row NFloat4 + DQ, column Mean

results.claim: Mean Pile Common Crawl perplexity is lowest for NFloat4+DQ, versus Int4.
results.setup: OPT, BLOOM, LLaMA, Pythia 125M-13B; Float4 E2M1 31.07, E3M0 29.48
results.table: Table 2, row NFloat4 + DQ, column Mean PPL

results.claim: RoBERTa-large on GLUE: QLoRA FP4 matches the 16-bit baseline.
results.table: Table 3, row QLORA FP4, column RoBERTa-large

results.claim: Applying LoRA to all linear layers is critical to match 16-bit performance; rank r does not matter.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B on Alpaca, RougeL, Fig 2 and Fig 4 (r in 8-64, 3 seeds per combination)

results.claim: Guanaco 33B scores 97.8% of ChatGPT on the Vicuna benchmark at 21 GB.
results.setup: Guanaco 33B 4-bit, GPT-4 judge, mean over both orders, 95% CI 4.4%

results.claim: A 9k-sample dataset (OASST1) beat a 450k-sample FLAN v2 subsample on chatbot performance.
results.setup: Vicuna and OA chatbot benchmarks; quality over size
results.quote: a 9k sample dataset (OASST1) outperformed a 450k sample dataset

results.claim: Guanaco 65B has an Elo of 1022 under GPT-4 judging on the Vicuna benchmark, second to GPT-4 (1348).
results.setup: GPT-4 judge, 10,000 random orderings; ChatGPT 966; human-rater Elo for Guanaco 65B is 1023 and ChatGPT 916

results.claim: Agreement between GPT-4 and human majority vote at the example level is weak.
results.setup: Vicuna benchmark, GPT-4 vs human annotators; system-level Kendall tau 0.43, Spearman 0.55; human-human kappa 0.42

results.claim: FLAN v2 does best on MMLU but worst on the Vicuna benchmark, so MMLU and chatbot quality are only partly related.
results.setup: LLaMA 65B finetuned on FLAN v2 with QLoRA; LLaMA 65B no tuning 63.4

results.claim: Training on the target only beats training on source and target for MMLU.
results.table: Table 10, row Train on target, column Mean

results.claim: Paged optimizers give the same training speed as regular optimizers for a 65B model on 48 GB at batch size 16.
results.setup: 65B, 48GB GPU, batch size 16; no hard measurements otherwise provided
results.quote: paged optimizers provide the same training speed

results.claim: Guanaco 65B has a lower CrowS bias score than LLaMA-65B.
results.setup: lower is less biased; GPT-3 67.2, OPT-175B 69.5

results.claim: 7.5% of 7B LLaMA hidden units fail the Shapiro-Wilk normality test at the 5% level.
results.setup: Shapiro-Wilk per hidden unit of LLaMA 7B weights; about 2.5% above expected false-positive rate

limits: The authors did not establish that QLoRA matches full 16-bit finetuning at 33B and 65B scales (Section 8).
Only MMLU, Vicuna and OA benchmarks were used; not BigBench, RAFT or HELM.
Chatbot benchmarks are called not trustworthy; Vicuna Table 6 has wide, overlapping confidence intervals and GPT-4 shows order effects and self-preference.
Only limited responsible-AI evaluation (CrowS); no other bit-precisions or adapter methods tested.
Paged optimizers not measured beyond one speed check.
Warmup, weight decay, epochs and token counts are not stated; Guanaco compared against baselines trained on proprietary data.

figures.caption: Different finetuning methods and their memory requirements. QLORA improves over LoRA by quantizing the transformer model to 4-bit precision and using paged optimizers to handle memory spikes.
figures.why: Shows full finetuning vs LoRA vs QLoRA memory at a glance.

figures.caption: RougeL for LLaMA 7B models on the Alpaca dataset. Each point represents a run with a different random seed.
figures.why: Shows LoRA on all layers is needed to match 16-bit.

figures.caption: Mean zero-shot accuracy over Winogrande, HellaSwag, PiQA, Arc-Easy, and Arc-Challenge using LLaMA models with different 4-bit data types.
figures.why: Shows NF4 beats FP4 bit for bit.
